title: Provider Conformance Profile v1
narrowingRule: No assertion may be satisfied by weakening a control, and no configuration option may relax an assertion at runtime. An implementation offering a flag that disables destination validation, policy consultation, or auditing is non-conformant regardless of that flag's default.

assertions.statement: All provider network I/O passes through a single chokepoint. No adapter calls the platform HTTP client directly.
assertions.procedure: Issue a normal request; assert the chokepoint was entered exactly once per attempt and no other network call occurred.
assertions.pass: No network egress observed outside the chokepoint.

assertions.statement: The destination is validated before each request is issued. An origin other than the configured endpoint is reachable only when the governing policy explicitly permits non-endpoint egress.
assertions.procedure: Under an endpoint-only policy, attempt a request to a non-configured origin.
assertions.pass: Rejected before any bytes are sent to that origin.

assertions.statement: Redirects are followed manually and every hop is re-validated and re-authorized. Delegating redirect following to the HTTP client is non-conformant.
assertions.procedure: Mock a 302 from the configured endpoint to a different origin under an endpoint-only policy.
assertions.pass: The request is not re-issued to the new origin; the denial is raised and audited.

assertions.statement: The redirect chain is bounded; exceeding the bound raises an error rather than silently returning the last response.
assertions.procedure: Mock a redirect loop longer than the documented bound.
assertions.pass: A named error is raised after the bound.

assertions.statement: Schemes other than http/https are rejected.
assertions.procedure: Attempt file:, ftp:, and data: endpoints, as configured endpoint and as redirect target.
assertions.pass: All rejected.

assertions.statement: URLs carrying embedded credentials (user:pass@host) are rejected.
assertions.procedure: Configure https://user:pass@host/v1 and redirect to the same shape.
assertions.pass: Both rejected.

assertions.statement: Loopback, private, link-local, carrier-grade-NAT, and multicast destinations are rejected unless the destination is the configured endpoint.
assertions.procedure: Redirect to 169.254.169.254 and to an RFC1918 address; separately configure http://127.0.0.1:<port>/v1 as the endpoint.
assertions.pass: Redirect targets rejected; the configured loopback endpoint is permitted.

assertions.statement: The set of permitted destinations is expressible as reviewable data (an allowlist), not only as code.
assertions.procedure: Inspect the implementation for a data-defined destination list.
assertions.pass: A reviewer can enumerate permitted destinations without reading control flow.

assertions.statement: Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization are stripped when a redirect crosses to a different origin.
assertions.procedure: Drive a same-origin redirect (headers retained) and a policy-permitted cross-origin redirect (headers stripped).
assertions.pass: Sentinel credential absent from the cross-origin request.

assertions.statement: Credentials never appear in audit records, logs, telemetry, error messages, or exception traces.
assertions.procedure: Search every artifact produced by the run for a sentinel credential value.
assertions.pass: Zero occurrences outside outbound request headers to the configured origin.

assertions.statement: The adapter persists nothing outside the lifetime of the request — not credentials, not request or response bodies.
assertions.procedure: Snapshot the filesystem and process state around a request.
assertions.pass: No new persisted artifact attributable to the adapter.

assertions.statement: Credentials are resolvable by indirection (environment variable or OS keychain reference) rather than requiring inline storage in configuration.
assertions.procedure: Configure a provider with an indirect key source only.
assertions.pass: The request succeeds without the secret appearing in any config file.

assertions.statement: Every attempt emits exactly one request record, whatever the outcome (ok / error / blocked).
assertions.procedure: Count records across success, transport error, HTTP error, and policy-blocked scenarios.
assertions.pass: Exactly one record per attempt in every scenario.

assertions.statement: The record identifies at minimum provider id, model id, destination origin, outcome, duration, and status code when one exists.
assertions.procedure: Inspect the field set of each emitted record.
assertions.pass: All required fields present and correct.

assertions.statement: Records carry no prompt text, completion text, tool arguments, file contents, or request/response headers.
assertions.procedure: Substring-search records for sentinel values planted in the prompt, the completion, and the headers.
assertions.pass: No sentinel found.

assertions.statement: A blocked request is recorded before the error is raised.
assertions.procedure: Trigger a policy denial and capture record ordering relative to the thrown error.
assertions.pass: The record exists even if the error propagates to the top of the run.

assertions.statement: Provider records join the same tamper-evident run log as the rest of the run, not a separate unchained provider log.
assertions.procedure: Verify the run chain after a mixed sequence of tool and provider events.
assertions.pass: Chain verification covers the provider records.

assertions.statement: A policy denial additionally emits a violation record naming the rule that denied it.
assertions.procedure: Trigger a denial and inspect for a violation record.
assertions.pass: The rule identifier appears in the record.

assertions.statement: The governing policy is consulted per request, not once at startup.
assertions.procedure: Mutate the policy between two requests in the same run.
assertions.pass: The second decision reflects the mutation.

assertions.statement: Policy is re-consulted at each redirect hop.
assertions.procedure: Redirect under a policy permitting the first origin and denying the second.
assertions.pass: The second hop is denied.

assertions.statement: An absent, malformed, or unreadable policy fails closed to a documented default and never silently degrades to unrestricted.
assertions.procedure: Supply a malformed policy source.
assertions.pass: The run is more restricted, not less, and the condition is surfaced.

assertions.statement: No adapter option, environment variable, or configuration field widens what the governing policy allows.
assertions.procedure: Enumerate every configuration surface the implementation exposes and attempt to widen policy through each.
assertions.pass: All refused. An unenumerated surface is a fail.

assertions.statement: Provider identity and model identity are checked against policy allowlists before the request is issued.
assertions.procedure: Request a denied model and a denied provider.
assertions.pass: Refused before egress.

assertions.statement: The policy in force is identified in the run record by a stable canonical hash.
assertions.procedure: Compare hashes across reordered but semantically identical policy files.
assertions.pass: Hash is stable for unchanged policy and changes when the policy changes.

assertions.statement: Streaming yields incremental text deltas whose concatenation equals the final content.
assertions.procedure: Replay a recorded response in streaming and non-streaming mode.
assertions.pass: Concatenated deltas equal the non-streaming content.

assertions.statement: Tool/function calls round-trip: streamed, fragmented tool-call arguments reassemble to exactly what the non-streaming path returns.
assertions.procedure: Split tool-call arguments across chunk boundaries mid-token and mid-UTF-8 sequence.
assertions.pass: Reassembled arguments are byte-identical to the non-streaming result.

assertions.statement: Transport, HTTP, and provider-level errors normalize to the runtime's error type; no provider-specific error object escapes the adapter.
assertions.procedure: Inject a 500, a malformed chunk, and a socket close mid-stream.
assertions.pass: All surface as the runtime's normalized error type.

assertions.statement: Cancellation stops the request promptly and still emits an audit record.
assertions.procedure: Abort mid-stream.
assertions.pass: The request stops and exactly one record is emitted.

assertions.statement: Token usage is reported when the provider exposes it, and reported as absent — never as zero — when it does not.
assertions.procedure: Replay responses with and without usage fields.
assertions.pass: Absent usage is distinguishable from zero usage.

assertions.statement: The adapter holds no cross-request state.
assertions.procedure: Interleave requests with conflicting configuration through one adapter instance.
assertions.pass: No cross-contamination of results.

assertions.statement: The suite runs fully offline against a mock transport. No test makes a real provider call.
assertions.procedure: Run the suite with network access removed.
assertions.pass: Suite passes unchanged.

assertions.statement: Every MUST assertion has at least one bypass test: remove the control and the test fails.
assertions.procedure: For each MUST, disable the control and re-run.
assertions.pass: The covering test fails. A suite that still passes is treated as not implementing the assertion.

assertions.statement: The same suite runs unmodified against every adapter, parametrized over the adapter registry.
assertions.procedure: Register an additional adapter and run the suite.
assertions.pass: No suite edits required.

assertions.statement: Adding an adapter requires no new bespoke governance test — passing the suite is the gate.
assertions.procedure: Review the contribution path for a new provider.
assertions.pass: The documented gate is the suite.

assertions.statement: The suite emits a report in the provider-conformance-report/v1 format.
assertions.procedure: Run the suite and inspect its output.
assertions.pass: A valid report document is produced.

result.bypassTest: boolean — required true for every MUST at the claimed level
result.evidence: stable pointer a reader can follow (test name, file:line, log id)

reportFormat.honestyRule: An unimplemented assertion is reported fail. It is never omitted, and never marked not-applicable unless the profile's applicability note covers the case.
